title: 1986 AHSME Problem 23
statement: Let \[ \begin{aligned} N={}&69^5+5\cdot69^4+10\cdot69^3\\ &{}+10\cdot69^2+5\cdot69+1. \end{aligned} \] How many positive integers are factors of \(N?\)

solutions.text:
By the binomial theorem, \[ \begin{aligned} N&=(69+1)^5=70^5\\ &=2^5\cdot5^5\cdot7^5. \end{aligned} \] A divisor independently chooses an exponent from \(0\) through \(5\) for each of the three primes. Thus \(N\) has \(6^3=216\) positive divisors.

Therefore the correct answer is E.
